reviews.one_line_contribution: Define per-item responsibility for a failed agent episode by seed-replicated removal re-runs (12 seeds, two 6-seed blocks, plus an emptied-set arm), then measure (a) how far cheap attributions - self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, single-seed leave-one-out - fall below a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate scored on the same episodes, (b) how often no single item is responsible at all, and (c) whether duplicating a culprit converts single into joint responsibility.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2608.20627, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic RAG' (AgenticRAG-FP), 2026-08-20, verified with the literature command (HF channel; s2cli paper 2608.20627 returned it). It is an interventional failure-attribution benchmark that injects a certified fault at a specified hop, re-executes the downstream trajectory, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known ground-truth fault - the same contribution shape as this proposal's E2 planted-culprit arm plus E3 method scoring, and it appears on the proposal's own novelty card while being absent from its Preprint Collision Check. It does not sink the proposal: its unit is a retrieval hop fault in multi-hop RAG, it has no seed replication (which is precisely this proposal's live axis, since ALFWorld outcomes are stochastic and a single re-run is a coin flip), no attributability rate over natural failures, and no joint-responsibility/duplication arm. Second threat: CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467 (verified, S2, 2 citations) already defines per-evidence-item utility by REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE interventions - the proposal's exact operator set - so the delta is 'same operators, multi-step stochastic agent, failure episodes', which reviewers will read as a setting transfer. Third: arXiv:2507.04480 'Source Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (PKDD/ECML Workshops 2025, 7 citations; direct `s2cli paper 2507.04480` returned 'not found', verified instead by title search on S2) already quantifies how well SHAP approximations mirror exact document attributions while minimizing costly LLM interactions - i.e. the accuracy-versus-cost frontier, one setting removed. Fourth, for the headline prediction specifically: arXiv:2605.29463 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (from the novelty card) already shows on ALFWorld that agents confidently mis-diagnose their own failures and act on the mis-diagnosis, which substantially deflates P1 ('self-report is a bad attributor') as a headline finding.
reviews.strongest_objection: The ceiling is selected on the same estimand it is supposed to bound, so the central gaps are partly manufactured. The scoring pool is defined as the episodes where the 12-seed one-sided 95% lower bound on max_i r_i clears zero - i.e. episodes pre-selected for a large, LOO-detectable removal effect (at m=12 this needs r_i of about 0.33, and the design's own power table implies the retained culprits mostly carry r of 0.5-0.7). The ceiling C is then a fresh 6-seed run of that same removal estimator. Disjoint seeds remove seed-level correlation but not the selection on the estimand: any removal-based estimator inherits a large true signal on this pool by construction, while self-report, confidence gain and position prior do not. P1, P2, P6 and P7 are all gaps against that one selected C (the entailment check flags the shared term), so the 20-25 point margins can be met without any of the cheap methods being bad in an unselected population - a reviewer will say the benchmark measures its own selection rule. The second half of the objection is P4, the claim that 'most memory-caused natural failures are not attributable to any single item': at 12 seeds the rule is blind to any true r below about 0.33, so a high non-attributability rate is largely a statement about the rule's power, not about the world, and it is the finding the abstract leads with. Releasing the r_i distribution mitigates but does not license the headline sentence.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Score the methods on an unselected pool as the primary analysis - every memory-caused failure, with a continuous criterion (rank correlation of each method's scores against the 12-seed r_i vector, or top-1 accuracy restricted to episodes where the label is well-determined by a criterion that is not the removal statistic itself) - and report the attributable-pool top-1 accuracies as the secondary, selection-inflated view; the planted-only oracle set, which is unselected, should carry P1-P3 by design rather than only as a fallback under the C-PP gate. (2) Restate P4 as a power-explicit statement ('fewer than X% have a single item with r >= 0.33') or, better, report the full distribution of max_i r_i with intervals as the headline instead of a thresholded rate. (3) Add the external LLM-diagnoser baseline (below); without it the method set contains no method the failure-attribution literature actually uses. (4) Fix the three predictions the entailment check flags: make the random tie-break the primary scoring of the m=1 point and pre-register P3a's falsifier as a fraction of the analytic single-seed ceiling implied by the E0 p(S); make P6's primary estimand the label-transfer rate on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, with the base-rate mismatch reported separately, or the arm measures backbone base rates rather than transfer of attribution; replace P5b's significance count with a pooled interaction magnitude and CI, since a 12%-versus-10% margin is far inside the cluster-bootstrap width at 6 seeds per subset. (5) Cite and position against arXiv:2608.20627 and arXiv:2605.29463 explicitly - a benchmark paper whose collision check omits the nearest interventional attribution benchmark will be read as not having looked.
reviews.missing_baseline: An external LLM diagnoser: a second call that sees the full failed trajectory plus the k retrieved items and names the responsible item (or 'none'). That is the method every prior failure-attribution paper evaluates (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338, the Who&When-style root-cause benchmarks, and the diagnosers scored in AgenticRAG-FP arXiv:2608.20627), and it is strictly stronger than the acting agent's own post-episode self-report, which is the only judge-like method in E3. Without it the paper claims that 'the cheap attributions current systems rely on' fail while omitting the cheap attribution the attribution literature actually relies on, and the self-report result is confounded with self-knowledge rather than diagnosability. A second, cheaper omission: an offline reuse estimator that scores items from episodes already in the k-sweep and nested-k logs (item present versus absent across games, with matching), which costs zero new episodes and is the natural 'do I need fresh re-runs at all' floor on the accuracy-versus-cost frontier the paper's headline figure claims to chart.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full claim, but the proposal's own check is incomplete in a way that matters for a benchmark paper. Channels: every query below was answered by the literature command (s2cli, S2 + HF, both ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries run: (1) --recent, 'attribute agent failure to individual retrieved memory item intervention re-run counterfactual ground truth benchmark' -> arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP, top hit), 2607.10608, 2607.13083, 2608.00017, 2509.10401, 2509.08682, 2602.16313 - nothing at item level with seed replication. (2) all-time, 'leave-one-out counterfactual removal of retrieved item stochastic policy seed replication noisy utility responsibility label' -> arXiv:2604.05467 (CUE-R), 2607.27888, 2605.25507, 2510.27484 (Thought Branches: resampling for causal analysis of reasoning - the same 'one run is not a counterfactual' argument, at the CoT-step level), 1909.10447 - no item-level agent-memory hit. (3) closest named method, 'CUE-R intervention based per evidence item utility remove replace duplicate RAG' -> arXiv:2604.05467 confirmed plus 2608.23252, 2605.01302 - all single-shot RAG. (4) home vocabulary, 'Shapley value data valuation stochastic noisy utility sample complexity ranking stability' -> Data Shapley 1904.02868, SVARM 2302.00736, shapiq 2410.01649 - the sample-cost-of-a-noisy-utility question is well developed there and the proposal does not engage it. (5) 'source attribution RAG Shapley contribution of each source document' -> arXiv:2507.04480 verified (S2, PKDD/ECML Workshops, 2025-07-06, 7 citations), matching the proposal's description. (6) --recent, 'does the model know which retrieved example it used self-report faithfulness counterfactual' -> 2602.02639, 2502.18156, 2601.10700 - classification/reasoning only, so the proposal's claim that self-report has never been tested against re-runs for retrieved items holds. IDs verified by direct lookup: 2604.05467, 2605.25338 (CausalFlow, 8 citations, step-level as described), 2607.10608, 2511.20857, 2602.16313, 2608.20627. Verified incidentally in search returns: 2509.10401, 2509.08682, 2607.13083, 2602.02639, 2502.18156. Verified by title search after a failed id lookup: 2507.04480. Not verified by me: 2507.05257, 2605.18565, 2604.20006, 2604.17658, 2509.23735, 2401.07927, 2307.08678, 2311.07466, and every id cited from the brief (2605.08374, 2608.02508, 2607.22562, 2607.21106, 2606.17628, 2603.04549). Judgement on the check itself: it is unusually specific and its three query classes are the right ones, and its negative conclusion survives my searches on the item-level-plus-seed-replication combination. But it names five papers under the mechanism query and omits arXiv:2608.20627, the single nearest interventional failure-attribution benchmark, which the proposal's own automated novelty card returned at sim 0.50 - the strongest evidence that the check was run before, and not reconciled with, the card. It also omits arXiv:2605.29463 (Honest Lying, ALFWorld self-diagnosis confabulation), which is directly on the headline P1 claim. Both omissions are the kind an area chair reads as a novelty argument that has not been closed.

reviews.one_line_contribution: It makes the retrieved memory item the unit of failure attribution in a multi-step agent, defines item responsibility operationally by seed-replicated removal re-runs (12 seeds, Newcombe interval, plus an emptied-set arm that asks whether memory caused the failure at all), and then uses those labels to measure how often the cheap attributions deployed memory systems actually rely on (self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, single-seed LOO) name the same item as a fresh intervention replicate does, at a stated re-run cost.
reviews.closest_prior_work: AgenticRAG-FP, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation' (arXiv:2608.20627, 2026-08-20; verified with s2cli paper and returned by my query 2 on both HF and S2). It is already an interventional benchmark for failure attribution built exactly the way this proposal builds its E2 arm: inject a certified retrieval fault at a chosen hop, re-execute the downstream trajectory, and score post-hoc diagnosers against the known injected cause, with propagation depth as an evaluation axis. It does not fully collide: its unit is a hop-level retrieval fault in single-episode agentic RAG, not a persistent retrieved experience item; it has no seed replication, no natural-failure labelling (its ground truth is planted, i.e. only the analogue of E2), no non-attributability estimand, and no accuracy-versus-cost frontier. But it removes most of the conceptual novelty of 'intervention as ground truth for attributing an agent failure to a piece of retrieved evidence', and it makes the planted-culprit half of this proposal a re-run of an existing benchmark in a new environment. Second closest: CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467, verified) already does per-evidence-item REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE with an evidence-role taxonomy, so the intervention primitives and even the duplication manipulation behind P5a are prior art in single-shot RAG; and CausalFlow (arXiv:2605.25338, verified, 8 citations) already does counterfactual causal responsibility scoring for LLM agent failures at step level. What genuinely remains unclaimed after these three is narrow: seed-replicated labels for a stochastic multi-step agent, the fraction of memory-caused failures attributable to no single item, and the measured gap between cheap attributors and an intervention replicate.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline result is close to being manufactured by the selection rule. Episodes enter the scoring pool only if the 12-seed leave-one-out procedure found an item whose removal effect clears r_i ~ 0.33; the ceiling C is a fresh 6-seed run of that same estimator, i.e. the same estimand computed by the same functional form as the label. Pairing and fresh seeds control label noise, which is what the Measurement section argues, but they do not control selection on the estimator: block C is guaranteed to see a large signal on exactly these episodes because that is why they were selected, while self-report, confidence gain, semantic overlap and the position prior are selected on nothing. So P1 (self-report >= 25 points below C) and P2 (confidence gain >= 20 below C) are largely a statement that a re-run of the labelling procedure reproduces its own label better than a different measurement does, on a set defined by that procedure. The reviewer will also note that the method set is a straw man: the actual state of the art in agent failure attribution is an LLM diagnoser over the trajectory (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, ErrorProbe arXiv:2604.17658, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338), and the actual attributions deployed memory systems use are learned item scores (MemQ Q-values, usage/survival scores, retrieval similarity) - none of which is scored here. Beating a position prior, a semantic-overlap heuristic and a forced-choice self-report does not establish that 'the cheap attributions current systems rely on' fail. Secondary but concrete: two of the seven predictions cannot be decided by the design as written (the proposal concedes P3b is low-power at +/-11.5 against a 10-point margin; P5b's falsifier sits 2 points above the nominal 10% false-positive rate, far inside the cluster-bootstrap CI, so it measures per-cell power at SE ~0.35, not additivity); P6 is confounded by backbone base rates, since scoring 'reader 2 succeeds at base' as disagreement on episodes selected because reader 1 failed produces the predicted 20-point gap from a base-rate difference alone; and P7's claim that 'regression to the mean is identical in both arms, so only the sentence can produce the gap' is wrong - a procedure sentence that raises p(S) mechanically compresses every r_i by ceiling, which is a second channel to the predicted drop in remain-attributable fraction and is not separated from substitution.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Break the circularity: define the primary scoring set by something other than the label estimator - score all attribution methods on the E2 planted/two-culprit set against the injected oracle as the confirmatory comparison (where the pool is defined by the plant, not by LOO), and demote the natural-episode gaps to a secondary, explicitly selection-caveated analysis; or select the natural pool by the emptied-set criterion (memory-caused) rather than by max_i r_i, and report method accuracy on all memory-caused failures with abstention scored, so a method is not required to reproduce an argmax that only the ceiling's own procedure can produce. (2) Add the two attributors that matter: an LLM post-hoc diagnoser reading the failed trajectory plus the k items (A2P/CausalFlow-style, with an abstain option) and at least one deployed learned item score (retrieval similarity, usage/recency-decay, MemQ-style Q-value) - these are the 'attributions current systems rely on' the abstract names. (3) Fix P6's estimand to label transfer on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, reporting base-rate mismatch separately. (4) Fix P7 by matching on base success (or reporting r_i normalised by headroom 1 - p(S)) so substitution is separable from ceiling compression. (5) Replace P5b's significance count with a pooled interaction magnitude and CI, and either drop P3b or extend block C to 12 seeds. (6) Cite and position against arXiv:2608.20627 explicitly, and state what the seed-replicated natural-failure labels buy over its injected-fault protocol. (7) Show the labels are worth 54 re-runs each by adding one downstream cell: demote/keep items under each attributor and measure the effect on subsequent success - otherwise this is a diagnostic with no demonstrated consumer.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. First, an LLM failure-diagnoser baseline: give a model the failed trajectory and the k retrieved items and ask it to name the responsible item (with 'none'), in the A2P / ErrorProbe / CausalFlow style - this is the method a reviewer will consider the real competitor to intervention, and the plan's 'self-report' (the actor's own post-episode account) is a much weaker proxy for it. Second, the memory system's own utility scores as attributors: retrieval similarity rank (beyond raw position), usage/recency decay, and one learned per-item score (MemQ-style Q-value or a DIG-style confidence-gain scorer trained on the stream) - the brief's Q1 asks for exactly one scorer per family, and their absence means the paper cannot support its own claim that deployed reinforcement/demotion scores are inaccurate. A cheaper third omission: a random-among-retrieved floor with abstention calibrated to the observed non-attributable rate, so the 'none' option is scored against a matched abstainer rather than against pure random choice.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim, but the proposal's own check is materially incomplete, and that counts against it. All six of my queries were answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok); WebSearch was unavailable and WebFetch is blocked, so no query used channel (b). Q1 (mechanism, --recent) 'attribute agent failure to responsible retrieved memory item counterfactual removal ground truth benchmark' returned 2607.10608 (Compliance Trap, trajectory-level), 2606.25449, 2509.23735, 2509.10401, 2507.05257, 2606.15903 - none item-level. Q2 (mechanism, --recent) 'interventional benchmark injected fault re-execution ground truth evaluate failure diagnosers retrieval agent' returned arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP) on both HF and S2, plus AgentDebugX 2607.18754, AgentCheck 2607.11098 (replay with injected faults), 2607.28802, 2601.06112, 2605.25338. Q3 (closest named method) 'leave-one-out intervention per-item utility of retrieved memory items agent episodes seed variance number of re-runs' returned CUE-R 2604.05467 and, notably, 'On Randomness in Agentic Evals' arXiv:2602.07150, which already establishes that single-run agentic estimates are variance-dominated and multiple runs are required - so the seed-replication premise is prior art, not a finding. Q4 (home literature, no agent/memory words) 'data valuation stochastic utility noisy leave-one-out Shapley Monte Carlo retraining variance rank stability' returned Data Shapley 1904.02868, shapiq 2410.01649 and nothing agentic - the seeds-to-label curve is a re-derivation of a known data-valuation phenomenon in a new setting. Q5 (--recent, self-explanation faithfulness) returned 2602.02639, 2502.18156 and 'Thought Branches' 2510.27484 (resampling-based causal analysis of reasoning), confirming the proposal's claim that self-report faithfulness has not been tested against counterfactual re-runs for retrieved items. Q6 (ALFWorld per-item memory ablation) returned VICT 2608.28128, MemHarness 2607.28272, MemQ 2605.08374 - credit at the action or set level, never the item. IDs I verified with s2cli paper or by direct return: 2608.20627, 2605.25338 (8 cit), 2604.05467, 2507.04480 (PKDD/ECML workshops, 7 cit), 2604.17658 (ACL; S2 title 'Towards Self-Improving Error Diagnosis in Multi-Agent Systems', consistent with ErrorProbe), 2509.10401, 2509.23735, 2507.05257, 2607.10608, 2602.02639, 2502.18156. IDs the proposal leans on that I did not verify individually: 2511.20857, 2602.16313, 2605.18565, 2604.20006, 2607.13083, 2401.07927, 2307.08678, 2311.07466. The substantive failure of the proposal's check is that it ran a --recent mechanism query and still missed arXiv:2608.20627, an interventional failure-attribution benchmark with certified injected faults and re-execution that has been on HF since 2026-08-20, three weeks before this brief - it is the nearest neighbour of the E2 arm and it is absent from both the Related Work and the Collision Check, while the check concludes 'no preprint provides item-level responsibility labels with seed replication'. That conclusion survives 2608.20627 on the natural-failure and seed-replication axes, so I do not call this a verified collision, but a novelty claim that missed the closest interventional attribution benchmark in the field has not been established by the proposal's own search - I established what remains of it, and it is narrower than claimed.

reviews.one_line_contribution: It defines the responsibility of an individual retrieved experience-memory item for an ALFWorld failure by seed-replicated re-runs with that item removed (12 seeds, two blocks, plus an emptied-set arm), and then scores cheap attribution proxies -- the agent's self-report, teacher-forced confidence gain, position prior, semantic overlap, single-seed leave-one-out, Shapley -- as a paired gap to a measured ceiling, the accuracy a fresh 6-seed intervention replicate attains against the same label. The genuinely new pieces are the unit (memory item rather than step, agent, document or set), the treatment of sampling noise as the estimand rather than a nuisance (seeds-to-label curve, split-half reliability, replicate-as-ceiling), and the attributability rate itself as a headline number.
reviews.closest_prior_work: VERIFIED, arXiv:2608.20627, 'When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic RAG' (2026-08-20; confirmed by s2cli paper and returned by two independent queries). It is already an interventional benchmark for causal failure attribution: it injects a certified fault at a specified hop, re-executes the downstream trajectory, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known fault, reporting 'broad evidence of post-hoc signal loss'. That is structurally E2 plus the headline framing of this proposal -- planted ground truth by re-execution, cheap diagnosers measured against it, and the finding that post-hoc attribution loses the signal. It does not sink the proposal outright: its unit is a retrieval hop in single-shot-answer agentic RAG rather than one of k co-retrieved experience items; its ground truth is injected, so it has no analogue of the natural-failure label, the attributability rate (P4), or the duplication/joint-responsibility arm (P5a); and it does not treat stochastic re-execution or the number of seeds as an estimand at all. The second threat is CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467, verified with s2cli paper: 'a lightweight intervention-based framework for measuring per-evidence-item operational utility in single-shot RAG'), whose REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE per-item intervention protocol is exactly the manipulation set here, one step short of the multi-step stochastic setting; the proposal's REMOVE-vs-token-matched-REPLACE ablation and its duplicated-culprit composition are CUE-R's perturbations transplanted. Third, arXiv:2507.04480 (verified: 'Source Attribution in RAG', PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations) already asks how well SHAP approximations mirror exact document attributions while minimising LLM calls -- i.e. the accuracy-versus-cost frontier, in single-shot RAG. Net: the mechanism, the ground-truth protocol and the cost-frontier framing all exist; what is new is the unit and the noise treatment. That is a real but incremental combination, not a new question.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claim is measured on a population selected to make it true, and that population is a small minority of the failures the paper says systems act on. Every method-versus-ceiling comparison (P1, P2, P3, P5b, P7) is scored only on 'attributable natural episodes' -- episodes the 12-seed rule certified as having one item with r_i >= about 0.33. By the proposal's own P4 that is at most 45% of memory-caused failures, which are themselves a fraction of the roughly 240 failures, leaving 60-110 episodes (the pre-registered extension guarantees only 80). So the result reads: on the roughly 8% of episodes where a single item has a huge, seed-stable effect, cheap proxies lag intervention. But a memory system that reinforces or demotes items on failure must decide on every failure, including the majority the benchmark declares unlabelable, and on those the benchmark supplies no target for any method -- so the number the paper produces does not answer the question the paper opens with. Compounding this, at n = 80 the paired accuracy CI is +/- 11.5 points while the falsifying margins are 15-25 points, so only enormous effects are decidable and the interesting negative (a proxy that matches intervention) cannot be certified either. Second-order but damaging in review: the entailment check's two near-entailments are real and both violate the brief's own 'no prediction entailed by a definition' rule. P6 scores 'reader 2 succeeds at base' as disagreement on episodes selected because reader 1 failed, so a plain base-rate gap between backbones produces the predicted 20 points with no failure of attribution transfer whatsoever; and P3a, with ties counted as abstention, has an arithmetic single-seed ceiling near p_culprit x (1 - p(S))^2, so '< 65%' is close to guaranteed by the scoring rule rather than by the science. P5b's falsifier sits 2 points above the nominal 10% false-positive rate with per-cell interaction SE around 0.35, which is not a test. Of seven predictions, one is the load-bearing open one (P1), one is the honest risky one (P2), and three are compromised.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, roughly in order of value. (1) Make the estimand the whole memory-caused failure population, not the attributable subset: release the full r_i vector per episode and score every method by rank correlation (or top-1-with-abstention calibrated against the released r_i distribution) over all failures, with the 'no single item is responsible' outcome as a first-class label rather than an exclusion criterion. That removes the winner's-curse selection, makes P4 a statement about the world rather than about the rule's 0.79 power, and roughly triples the usable n. (2) Audit the scorers the field actually deploys. The brief's Q1 names MemQ-style Q-values over a provenance DAG, RoMeRL-style utility coordinates, usage-decay survival and admission scores; the proposal scores none of them and instead evaluates self-report, confidence gain, position and lexical overlap. As written the paper cannot say anything about the memory systems it motivates itself with. (3) Repair P6 by conditioning: make the primary estimand label transfer on the subset where reader 2 also fails at base, and report the base-rate mismatch as a separate descriptive quantity. Repair P3a by pre-registering the falsifier as a fraction of the analytic single-seed ceiling computed from the E0 p(S), or by making the random tie-break primary. Replace P5b's significance count with the pooled interaction magnitude and its CI. (4) Re-run and re-position the collision check against arXiv:2608.20627, and state explicitly what the item-level, natural-failure, seed-replicated design buys over injected hop-level faults -- the paper needs that paragraph in the introduction, not in a rebuttal.
reviews.missing_baseline: A third-party LLM diagnoser: give an off-the-shelf model the failed trajectory, the task, and the k retrieved items, and ask it to name the culprit or abstain. This is the standard attribution baseline in every paper the proposal cites as related work (A2P arXiv:2509.10401, ErrorProbe arXiv:2604.17658, CausalFlow arXiv:2605.25338, the Who&When line, and the diagnosers scored in arXiv:2608.20627), it costs one call, and it is categorically different from the agent's own post-episode self-report, which is the only LLM-based method in E3. A reviewer will note that the proposal's own related-work section defines the field by these methods and then omits them from the comparison. Two cheaper omissions matter too: the retriever's own relevance score as a zero-cost ranking (the proposal has position and semantic overlap but not the score the retrieval system already computed, which is the first thing any practitioner would try), and at least one learned utility score from the brief's Q1 families. Note also that the proposal's static-procedure arm (E4) is a manipulation, not an attribution baseline, so it does not fill this hole.
reviews.preprint_collision: Not a verified collision on the central claim, but the check is materially incomplete and its closing sentence is wrong. The proposal asserts 'no preprint provides item-level responsibility labels with seed replication, a seeds-to-label curve, or an accuracy-cost frontier of attribution methods' after four queries, all in memory-item vocabulary, and it missed the nearest neighbour. Queries I ran, all answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok; WebSearch was unavailable this session and was not used): (1) mechanism, --recent, 'attribute agent failure to a specific retrieved memory item counterfactual removal intervention ground truth' -> arXiv:2607.13083, 2607.10608, 2608.00017, 2604.17658, 2604.05467, 2603.00026, 2509.23735, 2509.10401 -- overlaps the proposal's own list, nothing item-level with intervention labels. (2) mechanism, 'interventional benchmark injected fault re-execution evaluate failure diagnosers agentic retrieval' -> arXiv:2608.20627 (AgenticRAG-FP, 2026-08-20), plus arXiv:2607.11098 (AgentCheck, replay with injected faults), arXiv:2604.22708 (TraceElephant), arXiv:2603.25001, arXiv:2607.28802. 2608.20627 is the one that matters and the proposal does not cite it, though the automated novelty card surfaced it at sim 0.50; I verified it with 's2cli paper 2608.20627'. It already builds an interventional benchmark that injects a certified fault, re-executes, and scores post-hoc diagnosers against the known ground truth, reporting post-hoc signal loss -- so the proposal's E2 arm and its 'cheap attributions are much worse than intervention' framing are no longer new in kind, only in unit and in the seed-replication treatment. (3) closest named method, 'Shapley value attribution of retrieved documents source attribution RAG evidence utility' -> arXiv:2507.04480 verified (S2 metadata: PKDD/ECML Workshops, 7 citations; the s2cli 'paper' lookup on that id returned not-found, the search channel resolved it), plus arXiv:2512.05958 (MaxShapley, fair context attribution in generative search at 9x lower cost, 4 citations) which the proposal does not cite and which is a direct precedent for its accuracy-versus-cost frontier. (4) home vocabulary, 'variance and sample cost of leave-one-out data valuation noisy stochastic utility Monte Carlo Shapley replicates' -> only classical Data Shapley (1904.02868), shapiq, OddSHAP; nothing on stochastic-environment replication, so the noise angle is genuinely open. (5) 'leave-one-out removal of individual experience memory item agent success rate seeds variance' --recent -> nothing on item removal, but arXiv:2602.07150 ('On Randomness in Agentic Evals') already establishes that single-run agentic estimates carry large variance and need multiple runs, which pre-empts part of the seeds motivation at the eval level.
